raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- Local draft for human submission. Upload review-evidence.zip, replace the
     artifact note below with its public link, and complete the human review and
     final-main validation described in vllm-pr-submission-notes.md. -->

## Overview

Fuse the two routing layouts needed by Humming indexed experts when w13 and w2
select different row block sizes. On small SM90 batches, one Triton launch
replaces two alignment/count-and-sort chains while preserving both GEMM tiles.

Related: [#53911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53911) fuses DeepEP-v2
globalization with one alignment. This change handles two independently padded
layouts from already-globalized routes; deferred globalization keeps its existing
implementation.

## Claims

- Removes repeated routing work for small decode batches: the measured TP8 path
  uses one metadata kernel per layer instead of four, with no backend or tuning
  configuration change.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 8×H200, TP8, concurrency 1: approximately 5% lower
  TPOT, with 4.46% / 1.25% lower complete-request latency at 16K / 128K input.
- Uses existing alignment operations for other architectures and larger workloads.
  Equal block sizes continue sharing one alignment. No prefill, memory-saving,
  or DP+EP speedup is claimed.

## Validation

Tested against `6b3488cc97eed1f3b0414d84699e95c686723ebb`, using the same native
extensions, environment and checkpoint for both sources. Humming 0.1.19,
PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1; MRV2,
MXFP4 experts, FP8 KV, block size 64, Engram CPU offload, no speculative decoding
or prefix caching.

**End-to-end serving.** TP8, concurrency 1, 8192 batched tokens, 128 output tokens.
Each entry is the median of three per-round request means, four requests per round.
Timings are from unprofiled requests.

| Input tokens | Baseline TPOT (ms) | This PR (ms) | Reduction | Baseline request latency (ms) | This PR (ms) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16,384 | 6.721 | 6.346 | 5.58% | 1203.735 | 1150.028 | 4.46% |
| 131,072 | 6.309 | 5.990 | 5.04% | 3658.121 | 3612.308 | 1.25% |

The experiment used A1 / B / A2, including a return to the original source.
A1's 16K results drifted, so the table uses the faster control median for each
metric, rather than the slower first control. All rounds are retained.
Comparing the fastest control round with the slowest patched round still gives
5.39% / 3.66% lower TPOT at 16K / 128K. TPOT is a mean-per-request metric here,
not a token-latency p50.

**Mechanism.** A separate rank-0 trace over five decode steps shows routing
metadata launches decreasing from 800 to 200, including 200 calls to the new
kernel. Summed routing GPU time decreases from 2.067 to 0.309 ms. Other trace
categories also vary; these profile times are diagnostic, not end-to-end speedup.

**Operator and model checks.**

- Alignment suite: 677 passed, including 146 added cases covering route boundaries,
  invalid/nonlocal experts, local remapping, int32/int64 IDs, strided/offset
  inputs, padding and CUDA Graph replay after routes/maps change.
- Existing Humming routing, shape and output-buffer integration tests: 9 passed.
- Cold-L2 CUPTI under CUDA Graph, ABBA order, 200 samples per implementation:
  126 cases; all 60 fused cases improve 1.82–16.38×. The 66 reuse/fallback cases
  remain within approximately 2%. For 384 experts, six routes and blocks 8/40,
  the two layouts take 9.728 → 1.408 μs.
- TP8: 72 timed requests and 24 semantic checks succeed. A1/B match all eight
  semantic completion texts; maximum matched-token logprob difference is
  approximately 1.31e-4. These are smoke checks, not a full quality benchmark.
- 24 production-wrapper calls pass `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Generated code
  has no spills in the inspected six- and 64-route cases. Applicable local
  formatting, lint, typing and CI-selection hooks pass.

**DP+EP coverage.** Separate TP1/DP8/EP8 serving A/B tests use 1024 input and
256 output tokens, three rounds per concurrency. Default grouped C1/C8/C64 and
explicit indexed C1/C8/C16/C64 complete all 42 timed points, 2016 requests and
32 semantic checks. Every accepted arm passes GPU-isolation auditing.
Neither backend shows an attributable improvement: grouped bypasses this helper;
indexed selects equal w13/w2 tiles and already shares alignment. C1/C8 profiles
show zero paired-kernel launches. The small measured throughput differences
(-0.54% to +2.00%) are not reported as gains from this change.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and run variability</summary>

Run from the selected vLLM source checkout, with its matching native extensions
and `.venv`. Set `MODEL_PATH` to the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 checkpoint.
Run the baseline and patched source separately on otherwise idle GPUs.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD"
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH"
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$CUDA_HOME/lib64:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=1

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_align_block_size.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -q \
  -k 'humming_indexed_routing_matches_each_projection_tile or humming_gated_non_gated_shape_contract or humming_indexed_writes_supplied_output_buffer'
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe_align_block_size.py --paired
```

Start each serving arm with:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --max-num-seqs 48 --max-model-len 132096 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18041 --served-model-name dsv41 \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"./profiles","torch_profiler_with_stack":false}'
```

After `/health` succeeds, in a separate shell with the same environment:

```bash
ARM=baseline  # Use a distinct result directory for A1, B and A2.
for ISL in 16384 131072; do
  for ROUND in 1 2 3; do
    .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
      --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18041 \
      --model dsv41 --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
      --dataset-name random --random-input-len "$ISL" --random-output-len 128 \
      --random-range-ratio 0 --random-prefix-len 0 --ignore-eos \
      --num-prompts 4 --max-concurrency 1 --request-rate inf \
      --num-warmups 1 --seed "$((20261104 + ROUND))" \
      --extra-body '{"temperature":0}' --save-result --save-detailed \
      --result-dir "results/$ARM" --result-filename "isl${ISL}-r${ROUND}.json"
  done
done
```

TPOT mean-per-round min–max, milliseconds; all three rounds are included:

| Arm | 16K | 128K |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| A1: original | 7.262–7.866 | 6.234–6.318 |
| B: patched | 6.345–6.348 | 5.912–6.006 |
| A2: return to original | 6.710–7.088 | 6.364–6.626 |

Prepared evidence: `review-evidence.zip` contains per-round JSON, source hashes,
operator results, selected GPU traces, GPU-isolation records and reproduction
instructions. 

</details>

## Details

For `R = topk_ids.numel()`, the fused path requires SM90, `1 <= R <= 64`,
different positive block sizes and a maximum block size of 256. These bounds
limit the quadratic route comparison and padding initialization; they do not
depend on model name, weight dimensions, expert count, TP degree or weight dtype.

The kernel maps global to local expert IDs before grouping and ignores invalid
or nonlocal routes. It shares per-expert counts and route ranks, computes each
layout's padded offsets, and writes both layouts. It initializes all output padding on every
invocation, including graph replay. No device-to-host read or host synchronization
is introduced in the production wrapper.

The implementation stays in the existing alignment module, with a small Humming
call-site change. Weight padding, quantization, GEMM heuristics, backend defaults,
DeepEP deferred globalization and scatter retain their existing behavior. There
is no new environment variable or package dependency. Unlike
[#64978](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64978), which removes a count
load/fill from TritonExperts' alignment-free path, this prepares two layouts for
the existing indexed Humming GEMMs.

The alignment suite is added to the existing H100 CI job so CI can exercise the
SM90 path; existing MoE jobs cover fallback selection. Physical validation here
is H200 only. H100/non-SM90 hardware, DeepEP serving and a full model-quality
evaluation have not been run locally; upstream CI results are not yet available.

AI assistance was used for implementation, experiments, review and this text.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

   commands:

     - pytest -v -s kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py
     - pytest -v -s kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py

@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 import vllm._custom_ops as ops
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.moe_align_block_size import (
     moe_align_block_size,
+    moe_align_block_size_pair,
 )
 from vllm.triton_utils import triton
 from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
@@ -147,9 +148,116 @@ def benchmark_batched(
     return 1000 * ms, 1000 * max_ms, 1000 * min_ms
 
 
+def benchmark_paired_alignment():
+    """Compare two native alignments with paired dispatch using cold-L2 CUPTI."""
+    import json
+    import statistics
+
+    from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
+
+    cases = itertools.product(
+        [(1, 1), (1, 6), (2, 8), (8, 6), (8, 8), (13, 5), (512, 8)],
+        [16, 64, 384],
+        [(8, 40), (128, 32), (64, 64)],
+        [1, 2],
+    )
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    for (num_tokens, topk), num_experts, blocks, ep_size in cases:
+        topk_ids = torch.randint(
+            0, num_experts, (num_tokens, topk), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        expert_map = None
+        if ep_size > 1:
+            expert_map = torch.full(
+                (num_experts,), -1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+            )
+            local_experts = torch.randperm(num_experts, device="cuda")[::ep_size]
+            expert_map[local_experts] = torch.arange(
+                local_experts.numel(), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+            )
+
+        def baseline(
+            topk_ids=topk_ids,
+            blocks=blocks,
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            expert_map=expert_map,
+        ):
+            first = moe_align_block_size(
+                topk_ids,
+                blocks[0],
+                num_experts,
+                expert_map,
+                ignore_invalid_experts=True,
+            )
+            second = (
+                first
+                if blocks[0] == blocks[1]
+                else moe_align_block_size(
+                    topk_ids,
+                    blocks[1],
+                    num_experts,
+                    expert_map,
+                    ignore_invalid_experts=True,
+                )
+            )
+            return first, second
+
+        def paired(
+            topk_ids=topk_ids,
+            blocks=blocks,
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            expert_map=expert_map,
+        ):
+            return moe_align_block_size_pair(topk_ids, *blocks, num_experts, expert_map)

@@ -83,6 +83,18 @@ The `apply` method is where the implementations perform
 
 The core fused MoE implementation performs a series of operations. It would be inefficient to create output memory for each of these operations separately. To that effect, implementations are required to declare 2 workspace shapes, the workspace datatype and the fused MoE output shape as outputs of the workspace_shapes() method. This information is used to allocate the workspace tensors and the output tensor in `FusedMoEModularKernel::forward()` and passed on to the `FusedMoEExpertsModular::apply()` method. The workspaces could then be used as intermediate buffers in the fused MoE implementation.
 
+#### Indexed Humming routing
+
+Humming can select different row block sizes for its two expert projections.
+`moe_align_block_size_pair` prepares both routing layouts from the same top-k
+indices and expert map. On Hopper, batches of at most 64 routed rows with block
+sizes up to 256 use a single Triton launch. Other shapes and architectures use
+the existing alignment operator; equal block sizes share one alignment.
+This selection is independent of model dimensions and quantization format and
+requires no additional configuration. It does not change weight padding or GEMM
+tuning. DeepEP deferred globalization and scatter metadata retain their existing
+paths.
+
 #### finalize_weight_and_reduce_impl()
 
 It is sometimes efficient to perform TopK weight application and Reduction inside the `FusedMoEExpertsModular::apply()`. Find an example [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/20228). We have a `TopKWeightAndReduce` abstract class to facilitate such implementations. Please refer to the TopKWeightAndReduce section.

+@triton.jit
+def _moe_align_block_size_pair_kernel(
+    TopkIds,
+    ExpertMap,
+    SortedIds1,
+    ExpertIds1,
+    NumTokens1,
+    SortedIds2,
+    ExpertIds2,
+    NumTokens2,
+    NUM_ROUTES: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_EXPERTS: tl.constexpr,
+    TOP_K: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE_TOKEN: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE_TOPK: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE_MAP: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_SIZE1: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_SIZE2: tl.constexpr,
+    SORTED_SIZE1: tl.constexpr,
+    SORTED_SIZE2: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_EXPERT_MAP: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_ROUTES: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    route = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_ROUTES)
+    expert = tl.load(
+        TopkIds + route // TOP_K * STRIDE_TOKEN + route % TOP_K * STRIDE_TOPK,
+        route < NUM_ROUTES,
+        -1,
+    ).to(tl.int32)
+    valid = (route < NUM_ROUTES) & (expert >= 0) & (expert < NUM_EXPERTS)
+    if HAS_EXPERT_MAP:
+        expert = tl.load(ExpertMap + expert * STRIDE_MAP, valid, -1)
+        valid &= expert >= 0
+

+    earlier = (route[None, :] < route[:, None]) & valid[None, :]
+    rank = tl.sum((same_expert & earlier).to(tl.int32), 1)
+    count = tl.sum((same_expert & valid[None, :]).to(tl.int32), 1)
+    leader = valid & (rank == 0)

+    padded2 = tl.where(leader, tl.cdiv(count, BLOCK_SIZE2) * BLOCK_SIZE2, 0)
+    lower_expert = expert[None, :] < expert[:, None]
+    offset1 = tl.sum(tl.where(lower_expert, padded1[None, :], 0), 1)
+    offset2 = tl.sum(tl.where(lower_expert, padded2[None, :], 0), 1)
+
+    sorted1 = tl.arange(0, triton.next_power_of_2(SORTED_SIZE1))
+    sorted2 = tl.arange(0, triton.next_power_of_2(SORTED_SIZE2))
+    experts1 = tl.arange(
+        0, triton.next_power_of_2(triton.cdiv(SORTED_SIZE1, BLOCK_SIZE1))
+    )
+    experts2 = tl.arange(
+        0, triton.next_power_of_2(triton.cdiv(SORTED_SIZE2, BLOCK_SIZE2))
+    )
+    tl.store(SortedIds1 + sorted1, NUM_ROUTES, sorted1 < SORTED_SIZE1)
+    tl.store(SortedIds2 + sorted2, NUM_ROUTES, sorted2 < SORTED_SIZE2)
+    tl.store(ExpertIds1 + experts1, -1, experts1 < tl.cdiv(SORTED_SIZE1, BLOCK_SIZE1))
+    tl.store(ExpertIds2 + experts2, -1, experts2 < tl.cdiv(SORTED_SIZE2, BLOCK_SIZE2))

+    block2 = tl.arange(0, triton.next_power_of_2(triton.cdiv(NUM_ROUTES, BLOCK_SIZE2)))

+        expert[:, None],
+        leader[:, None] & (block2[None, :] < padded2[:, None] // BLOCK_SIZE2),
+    )
+    tl.store(NumTokens1, tl.sum(padded1, 0))
+    tl.store(NumTokens2, tl.sum(padded2, 0))

+def moe_align_block_size_pair(
+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    block_size1: int,
+    block_size2: int,
+    num_experts: int,
+    expert_map: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> tuple[
+    tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
+    tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
+]:
+    """Align the same routes for two independently tuned MoE projections.
+
+    Each result has the semantics of ``moe_align_block_size`` with
+    ``ignore_invalid_experts=True``. Equal block sizes share one result.
+    Small Hopper batches use one launch; other batches use the existing op.
+    """
+    if block_size1 == block_size2:
+        alignment = moe_align_block_size(
+            topk_ids.contiguous(),
+            block_size1,
+            num_experts,
+            expert_map,
+            ignore_invalid_experts=True,
+        )
+        return alignment, alignment
+
+    num_routes = topk_ids.numel()
+    # Bound the quadratic route comparison and per-CTA padding initialization.
+    if not (
+        current_platform.is_cuda()
+        and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(90)
+        and 0 < num_routes <= 64
+        and max(block_size1, block_size2) <= 256
+    ):
+        alignments = [
+            moe_align_block_size(
+                topk_ids.contiguous(),
+                block_size,
+                num_experts,
+                expert_map,
+                ignore_invalid_experts=True,
+            )
+            for block_size in (block_size1, block_size2)
+        ]
+        return alignments[0], alignments[1]
+
+    outputs = []
+    for block_size in (block_size1, block_size2):
+        max_num_tokens_padded = min(
+            num_routes * block_size, num_routes + num_experts * (block_size - 1)
+        )
+        outputs.append(
+            (
+                torch.empty(
+                    max_num_tokens_padded, device=topk_ids.device, dtype=torch.int32
+                ),
+                torch.empty(
+                    triton.cdiv(max_num_tokens_padded, block_size),
+                    device=topk_ids.device,
+                    dtype=torch.int32,
+                ),
+                torch.empty(1, device=topk_ids.device, dtype=torch.int32),
+            )
+        )
+    _moe_align_block_size_pair_kernel[(1,)](
+        topk_ids,
+        expert_map,
+        *outputs[0],
+        *outputs[1],
+        num_routes,
+        num_experts,
+        topk_ids.size(1),
+        *topk_ids.stride(),
+        expert_map.stride(0) if expert_map is not None else 1,
+        block_size1,
+        block_size2,
+        outputs[0][0].numel(),
+        outputs[1][0].numel(),
+        expert_map is not None,
+        triton.next_power_of_2(num_routes),
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    return outputs[0], outputs[1]
